e through the API\nitself: `GET /projects` lists your projects, `GET /projects/{projectId}/servers`\nlists each project's servers,
and `GET /projects/{projectId}/eval-suites`\nlists its eval suites. Start from `GET /me` to confirm which account a key\nacts as.

## Errors

Errors always use the canonical body `{ code, message, details? }`. The `code`
is stable and machine-readable; `

message` is human-readable and may change;
`details` is an optional, unstructured bag.

| Code | HTTP | Meaning |
| - | - | -
|\n| `UNAUTHORIZED` | 401 | Missing, invalid, revoked, or orphaned key |\n| `OAUTH_REQUIRED` | 401 | The **target MCP server** nee
ds an OAuth grant; distinct from a bad key |\n| `AUTH_REQUIRED` | 403 | The **target MCP server** allowed the connection and asked
for sign-in on this call. `details.authChallenge` carries the parsed challenge. Your key is fine; see [Sign-in challenges](#sign-
in-challenges) |\n| `FORBIDDEN` | 403 | Key is valid but not allowed to do this, or the **target MCP server** rejected the credent
ials MCPJam presented (retrying with a different MCPJam key will not help; reconnect or re-authorize the server) |\n| `VALIDATION_
ERROR` | 400 | Malformed body or parameters |\n| `NOT_FOUND` | 404 | Unknown project, server, or resource |\n| `CONFLICT` | 409 |
The resource isn't in a state that accepts this write, such as a stale `expectedRevision`, a duplicate name, or an environment tha
t can't currently be launched. Re-read and retry |\n| `FEATURE_NOT_SUPPORTED` | 422 | The target server doesn't support this MCP c
apability |\n| `RATE_LIMITED` | 429 | Too many requests; see [Rate limits](#rate-limits) |\n| `SERVER_UNREACHABLE` | 502 | Could n
ot connect to the target MCP server |\n| `TIMEOUT` | 504 | The target MCP server connected but didn't respond in time |\n| `INTERN

AL_ERROR` | 500 | Something failed on our side |

New error codes may be **added** over time; treat unknown codes as
non-retrya

ble failures unless the HTTP status says otherwise.

### Sign-in challenges

Some MCP servers allow the connection and ask for

sign-in only on a protected
call. The API never starts a sign-in. It reports the challenge instead:

* **HTTP 401 from the MCP
server** on `tools/call`: the API answers\n `403 AUTH_REQUIRED`. `details.authChallenge` carries the parsed challenge:\n its `s
ource` (`http_401`), and the `error`, `requiredScope`, and\n `resourceMetadataUrl` the server sent, when present.\n* **An `isErro
r` result carrying `_meta[\"mcp/www_authenticate\"]`** (the\n ChatGPT convention): the call succeeds, and the `CallToolResult` is
returned\n unchanged with an additive `authChallenge` field (`source:\n \"tool_result_meta\"`). A field the server already set

under that name is never
 overwritten.

`AUTH_REQUIRED` is not `UNAUTHORIZED`: your MCPJam key is fine, so a different
key wi
ll not help. Complete the OAuth flow for that server yourself, upload the\ntoken to one of its [accounts](#server-accounts), and c

all again. See
[Mid-session sign-in](https://docs.mcpjam.com/inspector/lazy-authentication.md).

## Rate limits

Each key get
s **60 requests per minute** sustained, with bursts up to **10**.\nExceeding it returns `429 RATE_LIMITED` with a `Retry-After` he

ader (in
seconds):

```http theme={"theme":"css-variables"}
HTTP/1.1 429 Too Many Requests
Retry-After: 7

{ "code":

xponential backoff, and expect these limits
to be tuned during the preview.

Other `429`s, the per-minute brakes and daily budg
ets described with the\nendpoints below, carry `Retry-After` whenever the refusal knows when it\nlifts, which is the ordinary case
. Treat it as a hint that is usually there\nrather than a guarantee: a refusal that reaches you without one still needs\nyour back

off, so **never** block waiting for a header that may not come.

## Endpoints

Each endpoint is fully documented (request and

response schemas, examples,
and an interactive playground) under **Endpoints** in the sidebar.

**Catalog**: discover the IDs e

verything else takes:

| Endpoint | What it does |
| - | - |
| `GET /me` | The account behind the key |
| `GET /organizations
` | The organizations the caller belongs to, where `organizationId` comes from. A key is bound to one organization and only ever s
ees that one |\n| `GET /projects` | Projects the key can access (optionally `?organizationId=`) |\n| `GET /projects/{projectId}/se
rvers` | The project's saved MCP servers |\n| `GET /projects/{projectId}/servers/{serverId}/revisions` | A server's stored revisio
ns, newest first: captures of its tools and server info, recorded whenever they change (`?limit=&cursor=`) |\n| `GET /projects/{pr
ojectId}/servers/{serverId}/revisions/{revisionNumber}` | One revision: every tool's definition and the server info it reported. F
ields listed in `droppedFields` were too large to store, so they are unknown, not absent |\n| `GET /projects/{projectId}/servers/{
serverId}/revisions/{revisionNumber}/diff` | What changed since the revision before, or since `?from=`: tools added, removed and c
hanged, and server info changes with both values. A field listed in `droppedFields.from` or `droppedFields.to` was not stored on t
hat side, so a change to it is unknown |\n| `GET /projects/{projectId}/eval-suites` | The project's eval suites, with latest-run s
ummaries |\n| `GET`, `POST /projects/{projectId}/clients` | List clients, or create one from a template or full config |\n| `GET`,
`PATCH`, `DELETE /projects/{projectId}/clients/{client}` | Read, edit, or delete a client. The path segment takes a client **name
or ID** |\n| `POST /projects/{projectId}/clients/{client}/servers` | Replace the client's server attachments (a replacement; omit
ted servers are detached) |\n| `POST /projects/{projectId}/clients/{client}/duplicate` | Copy a client's current config into a new

client |
| `GET /chat-sessions` | Chat sessions (`?projectId=&status=&limit=&before=`) |

**Project environments**: the named
execution bundles (one host, optionally a\nstandalone server group) that eval suites and goals run against. Reads need\nproject me
mbership. Archiving needs project admin and is revisioned: pass the\n`revision` you last read back as `expectedRevision`, and a st

ale value returns
`CONFLICT` (409).

| Endpoint | What it does |
| - | - |
| `GET /projects/{projectId}/environments` | List
environments (`?includeArchived=true` to include archived ones) |\n| `GET /projects/{projectId}/environments/{environmentId}` | Re
ad one environment |\n| `GET /projects/{projectId}/environments/{environmentId}/resolve` | Preview the host config and closed serv
er set this environment resolves to right now |\n| `POST /projects/{projectId}/environments/{environmentId}/archive` | Archive it.
The environment is kept, and its name is freed for a new one |\n\n**Server diagnostics & primitives** (`/projects/{projectId}/ser

vers/{serverId}/...`):

| Endpoint | What it does |
| - | - |
| `POST .../validate` | Connect, initialize, and capture a capab
ility snapshot |\n| `POST .../doctor` | Full health workflow: probe → connect → initialize → capabilities |\n| `POST .../check-oau
th` | Does this server require an OAuth grant? |\n| `POST .../tools` | List the server's tools |\n| `POST .../tools/call` | Execut
e a tool; returns the MCP `CallToolResult` plus additive `durationMs`, and `authChallenge` when the result asks for sign-in (see [
Sign-in challenges](#sign-in-challenges)) |\n| `POST .../prompts` | List the server's prompts |\n| `POST .../prompts/get` | Render
a prompt; returns the MCP `GetPromptResult` verbatim |\n| `POST .../resources` | List the server's resources |\n| `POST .../resou
rces/read` | Read one resource by URI |\n| `POST .../export` | One JSON snapshot of tools, resources, and prompts |\n| `GET`, `PUT
`, `PATCH`, `DELETE .../accounts[/{account}]` | The server's accounts. See [Server accounts](#server-accounts) |\n| `POST .../oaut
h/import-tokens` | **Deprecated.** Uploads to your default account; use `PUT .../accounts/{account}`. See [The deprecated import r

oute](#the-deprecated-import-route) |

**Eval runs** (`/projects/{projectId}/...`):

| Endpoint | What it does |
| - | - |
|
`POST .../eval-suites` | Author-only: create a suite + its test cases from `name` + `serverIds` + a default `model` + `tests`, WI
